item.title: A house for the theory, a voice for the slides
item.description:
Every long thought eventually needs two things: a house and a voice. A house, so you can walk from room to room and see how the ideas connect. A voice, so someone can stand at the door and tell you what is inside before you commit to reading the whole thing.

flove has both in the making. The slides are the most precious material we have — years of thinking, drawn by hand, page after page, dense in the way a seed is dense. They are also, by nature, hard to enter: you have to already know where to look. The videos are the introduction — a spoken, visual doorway into that material. The last stretch of work was, in the most literal sense, preparation for those videos: building the house the slides will live in, labelling the shelves, and wiring the first room so the voice has somewhere to speak from.

item.title: The tag cloud and the playlist: how Risa's frontend grew up
item.description: Risa is, at heart, two pieces of frontend. On the left, a floating cloud of tags — little chips that drift around, that you tap to filter the feed, that grow when you ask them to. On the right, the playlist — the player, the threads, the reactions, everything that happens when a laugh is actually listened to. Over the last month that frontend went through three lives: it was born, it was moved into a shared engine, and it was cleaned until anyone could fork it. This is the story of those two pieces across the versions — and the three names you need to keep straight: flove0 (the distro), risa1 (nick as tag), risa2 (the current one, on the shared libraries).
